voyage.name: Arena
voyage.hours: Open daily from 08:30 to 19:00, but closes early if there's a performance that evening
voyage.content: An enormous, spectacular Roman amphitheatre, crumbling on the outside but still in use today. It was erected in the 1st century AD in an elliptical shape, and is the world's third-largest amphitheatre to survive from antiquity. The outer wall fell down during the earthquake of 1117, except for a small section locally called the "Ala" or wing, and enterprising citizens used the rubble to build houses on the back of th

voyage.name: Castelvecchio
voyage.price: Free to explore the grounds, €6 (€4.50 for seniors) to visit the museum and climb on the ramparts (cash or card)
voyage.content: A 14th-century, red brick, fortified castle on the banks of the river Adige. The main castle buildings house the city art museum which is packed with a rich collection of medieval sculpture and Renaissance paintings. As well as the museum, the extensive castle ramparts are great for exploring - ideal for families with children who enjoy running around castle fortifications. The Castelvecchio has an adjoining bridge o

voyage.name: Piazza delle Erbe
voyage.content: Home of the Forum in Roman times, this is still a focal point of the city. Contains the 'Britney Verona' fountain, 14th-century 'Gardello Tower', and a market that, while picturesque, seems to have become another tourist cliche during its refurbishment.

voyage.name: Lamberti Tower
voyage.content: completed in 1463, this is the tallest of Verona's towers. The distinctive clock tower looms over the Piazza delle Erbe, and you enter via the palace courtyard. 238 steps to the top, or take the lift, for great views. Ticket also includes admission to the Modern Art Gallery - but this is closed Monday and price is reduced.

voyage.name: Porta Borsari
voyage.content: The remains of a Roman gate, dates to at least the 2nd century AD, but is almost certainly older.

voyage.name: Verona Cathedral
voyage.price: Free entry to the cathedral, €3 for the archaeological exhibition
voyage.content: It was built to replace an 8th-century church which was destroyed in the earthquake of 1117. Consecrated in 1187, the church features an ornate marble Romanesque façade by the Veronese architect Nicolò; its pillars are supported by two griffins. Stone reliefs around the door include Biblical scenes. The smaller side door is also worth a look - medieval carvings include Jonah being swallowed by a whale. Inside, the na

voyage.name: Basilica of St Zeno
voyage.content: A 10-minute walk NE of Castellvecchio. The church is dedicated to Verona's patron saint, Zeno, a 4th-century North African and a keen fisherman who was ordained Bishop of Verona in 363. Zeno's tomb lies in a shrine in the church undercroft, and he is also commemorated in a grinning medieval statue in full episcopal robes, dangling a golden fish on the end of a fishing rod. The entrance to the church is graced with an

voyage.name: Chiesa di Sant'Anastasia
voyage.content: Richly decorated in 13th-15th century Gothic style. Note especially the Pelligrini Chapel, with the Pisanello depiction of St George setting off to fight the dragon.

voyage.name: Chiesa di San Giorgietto
voyage.content: A tiny chapel immediately next to Sant'Anastasia. Easily overlooked, this church is richly decorated with early Renaissance frescoes depicting the walled garden of the Virgin Mary.

voyage.name: Casa di Giulietta
voyage.content: Presented as the location of the famous balcony love scene from Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet (which wasn't even in the original version), the house is a major destination for tourist pilgrimage, as the tiny and usually crowded courtyard is normally packed with love-struck teenagers photographing each other on the famous balcony. Shakespeare's characters were fictional, but the house used to belong to the Capello fa

voyage.name: Casa di Romeo
voyage.content: So, if Juliet lived there, what about Romeo? A couple of streets away another house has been designated as his home. It is private, so other than a sign on the wall there is nothing much to see.

voyage.name: Juliet's Tomb
voyage.content: The church also houses the Antonian Fresco Museum.

voyage.name: Castel San Pietro
voyage.hours: Closed for restoration as of Oct 2019
voyage.content: This former Austrian barracks dates back to the Austrian occupation of the left bank, and while the building is not open to the public, the views from the hill over Verona are spectacular. Nice sunset views.

voyage.name: Giardino Giusti
voyage.content: One of Italy's most important Renaissance/mannerist gardens, with grottoes, fire-breathing masks carved into the hillside, etc.

voyage.name: Fort Wohlgemuth & World War I Museum
voyage.content: The fort was built between 1850 and 1851 on the Mount Castle (227 m), north-west of Rivoli. The fort hosts a museum on World War I and on vintage radios.

voyage.name: Lamberti tower
voyage.content: Climb to the top of it or take the lift. Great views over Verona.

voyage.name: S. Maria di Lourdes Sanctuary
voyage.content: Breathtaking view from the edge of Verona's highest hill.

voyage.name: Amarone wine tour
voyage.address: Via Vigolo, 16 Negrar di Valpolicella 37024 Verona
voyage.content: Discover the Valpolicella wine region with the famous Amarone.

voyage.name: Minigolf La Torretta
voyage.content: Fun activity for the entire family. Good alternative for children when tired of sightseeing. Great panoramic view of the hills around Verona.

voyage.name: Via Mazzini
voyage.content: Verona's golden mile of shopping, taking you between Piazza Bra and Piazza delle Erbe. Most of the major Italian labels are represented, and even if you can't afford them it is great to wander and window shop.

voyage.name: Corso Porta Borsari
voyage.content: is another elegant shopping street in Verona, eg Lo Scrittoio, an old-fashioned shop selling papery and elegant pens and pencils.

voyage.name: Corso Santa Anastasia
voyage.content: This street is the centre of the antiques shops' zone. Narrow streets where you can find authentic masterpieces.

voyage.name: Eurospar
voyage.content: A large two-storey supermarket with normal prices where you can find everything for your picnic.

voyage.name: Pizzeria da Vincenzo
voyage.content: Traditional pizzeria. Best pizza. Their secret is special flour... Small and cozy place, good service.

voyage.name: Buoono
voyage.content: In this place they make excellent wraps, very good doughs, both normal and wholemeal, the ingredients for the filling are delicious and of excellent quality. The food is very good, most likely the best piadineria in the area.

voyage.name: La Tradision
voyage.content: The place is very good and the varieties of cold meats as well. Cicchetti (like tapas) are tasty. Typical place for aperitifs with many appetizers.

voyage.name: Piadineria Artigiana Bacchabundus Cavour
voyage.content: Very good piadina and great choice. Very nice place, excellent wraps, very kind and helpful staff. Wide variety of vegetarian / vegan options.

voyage.name: Ristorante Cinese La Pagoda
voyage.content: Excellent Chinese restaurant with good food. Excellent care in treating the ingredients. The shrimps are superb. The chicken is also tender and well marinated. One of the first Chinese restaurants opened in Verona since the 80s.

voyage.name: Trattoria Trota da Luciano
voyage.content: To eat real traditional and homemade Italian cuisine. Typical trattoria. Generous portions and impeccable service.

voyage.name: Pizzeria La Conchiglia
voyage.content: Crispy and melting thick crust pizza. Big, fluffy and very tasty slice. It's right next to the arena.

voyage.name: Osteria Trattoria Al Duomo
voyage.price: Menus are not overpriced, about €15-20 a head (plus wine)
voyage.content: Excellent family-run restaurant, just next to the Cathedral (as its name suggests). It's popular with the local Veronese (a good sign) and with a menu full of traditional local specialities. You'll find this is a good place to blend in with the local scene, and has welcoming staff who will help you with unfamiliar items on the menu. On Wednesdays, Al' Duomo plays host to a local mandolin ensemble, so if you're on a t

voyage.name: Osteria Al Carroarmato
voyage.content: A charmingly atmospheric and good value restaurant/wine bar in the 'ancient canteen' style with shared tables and paper place mats. Food is authentically Veronan but unpretentious. There is an enormous, equally good value wine list, which can however rise to meet all budgets.

voyage.name: Signorvino
voyage.price: €12 mains. You pay the same price for wine in the restaurant as in the store
voyage.content: Restaurant and wine shop. Good food and great wines at very reasonable prices (wine at the table cost the same as in the shop). You eat either inside between wine racks or outside at one of 5 small tables. The menu consists of dishes from different regions of Italy.

voyage.name: Ristorante Flora
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant. The dining room is spacious, the staff friendly and the food really good.

voyage.name: Piazza Bra bars
voyage.content: Eat gelato there.

voyage.name: Caffè delle Erbe
voyage.content: Great coffee and brioche.

voyage.name: Rain
voyage.content: A wine bar and jazz club in the heart of Verona owned by brothers Giuseppe and Riccardo Zambelli Rain. Giuseppe is fluent in English. Ask for him if you have any questions about the area.

voyage.name: Campeggio Castel San Pietro
voyage.content: Spectacular views over the city and about 15 minutes walk from the centre. Peaceful, luxuriant vegetation. Also cabins and tents-for-rent offered.

voyage.name: Agriturismo Sommavalle
voyage.content: In the Torricelle suburb north of Verona, 4 km from the historical centre; it occupies a sunny and panoramic area on the southern side of a hill about 300m above sea level. It can be easily reached by car or with the urban bus service. Reaching the train station (Verona Porta Nuova) will take about 20 minutes by car.

voyage.name: Apple Suite B&B
voyage.price: Rates from €80 depending on length of the stay
voyage.content: Full apartment, gentle host, in the heart of city centre.

voyage.name: B&B Mambrotta
voyage.content: 14 km from the center of Verona, and 2 minutes from autostrada A4 Verona Est exit, in a quiet and wonderful environment of Venetian plain, in Mambrotta village. It's 20 minutes by car to Opera of Arena of Verona and to Soave town, it's 18 minutes by car to Verona fair show and exhibitions.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Verona
voyage.content: An elegant aristocratic building decorated with paintings and sculptures of some of the best Italian artists of the 20th century, for this luxury four-star hotel of Verona. From the Grand Hotel one can easily reach by walk the famous Arena and the other monuments of the historic centre of Verona.

voyage.name: Hotel Gardenia
voyage.address: Via Unità d’Italia 350, San Michele Extra
voyage.content: High quality service with rooms from around €80.

voyage.name: Hotel Italia Verona
voyage.content: Large meeting room, restaurant. An economical three-star hotel.

voyage.name: Agriturismo Ca' del Ferro
voyage.content: Rooms are very cosy and spacious and the owner is very helpful and friendly. You need to have a car though to reach it and move around. Single rooms at €45-€50 and double rooms from €75. They all have private beautiful coloured bathrooms.

voyage.name: Agriturismo Delo Relais
voyage.content: A charming farmhouse a few kilometers away from Verona city center in the Veneto hills. The property features 4 standard rooms, 2 junior suites and 2 suite.

voyage.name: Hotel Gabbia d’Oro
voyage.content: This is a lovely place, de luxe rooms in an 18th-century palazzo.
